prompt: Run two independent lookups as separate CompletableFutures and fold them into one answer with thenCombine. Complete quoteCents and quoteLabel, then run the tests.
explanation: supplyAsync hands a Supplier to a background thread and immediately returns a CompletableFuture, so starting two of them lets both pieces of work overlap. thenCombine waits for both futures and applies a BiFunction to their results, producing a third future -- no manual joining or shared arrays needed. thenApply adds another transformation stage on top, and only join() at the very end blocks the calling thread to pull the finished value out.
hints: CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> itemCents * quantity) starts the first piece of work; make a second one the same way for shipping.
first.thenCombine(second, (a, b) -> a + b) gives you a CompletableFuture<Integer> holding the total -- call join() on it to get the int.
For the label, keep the combined future and chain .thenApply(cents -> String.format(...)) before join(), so both methods share the same two-future structure.
